prompt: Consider the claim: "If a positive whole number is divisible by $3$, then it is divisible by $6$." Give the SMALLEST positive whole number that is a counterexample.
hint: You need a number that passes the "if" part but fails the "then" part.

hints.text: You need a number that passes the "if" part but fails the "then" part.
List multiples of 3: $3, 6, 9, 12, \dots$ Which is the first one that is NOT a multiple of 6?
$3$ itself: it is divisible by 3 but not by 6.

explanation: A counterexample must satisfy the hypothesis (divisible by 3) and break the conclusion (divisible by 6).
The multiples of 3 are $3, 6, 9, 12, 15, \dots$; the very first one, 3, is not divisible by 6.
So $3$ is the smallest counterexample, and the claim is false.

alternativeExplanations.title: Odd multiples give it away
steps: Every multiple of 6 is even, but multiples of 3 alternate odd and even: 3, 6, 9, 12.
Any ODD multiple of 3 breaks the claim — 3, 9, 15 all work — and the smallest of those is 3.
